reason: Stipuler que teaches a formal text-as-subject construction and must be distinguished from people agreeing terms with convenir de.
Étayer a claim with evidence materially corrects the unrelated legacy gloss and teaches useful argument government.
Supposer or conjecturer preserves a tentative inference and replaces the nonexistent old_back surmettre.
Vanter captures insistent promotional praise and corrects the false-friend legacy copy tout.
Valider is a transparent, high-frequency cognate, while the bare prompt does not select technical verification, institutional approval or emotional validation.
Vénérer is a transparent formal cognate with no distinctive construction or interference risk in this context-free prompt.
Vilipender teaches the strongly condemnatory, polemical force that distinguishes vilification from ordinary criticism.
Justifier an action or conclusion fixes the evidence-grounds sense and corrects legacy garantir, which belongs to guarantee senses.
Affirmation versus formal assertion and unproved allégation provides a useful evidential and register distinction.
Croyance is familiar C1 vocabulary, and the isolated prompt does not distinguish conviction, religious belief or an unsupported assumption.
Concept is a transparent, high-frequency academic cognate with nothing distinct to teach in a bare noun prompt.
La thèse défendue captures a claim being advanced and corrects the false friend contestation, which means challenge or protest.
Analyse critique fixes the structured-evaluation sense instead of leaving critique ambiguous between criticism and a review.
The reasoning term is retained to teach the precise distinction between logically entailed déduction and broader, defeasible inférence.
Dogme is a transparent formal cognate already available to a C1 learner, with no construction or specialized sense supplied.
Éclaircissement is more idiomatic for explanatory clarification, while old_back élucidation is tilted toward solving a crime or mystery.
L’accent mis sur teaches the productive French frame and avoids both emphase and the semantically different legacy mise en évidence.
Hypothèse is a transparent, high-frequency academic cognate, and the bare prompt adds no distinctive government or sense.
Inférence is useful formal reasoning vocabulary whose defeasible scope contrasts with the retained deduction card.
French has no single general equivalent; éclairage captures evidence-based analytical understanding better than legacy intuition.
Interprétation is a transparent, familiar cognate, and the source provides no context selecting explanation, performance or textual reading.
Jugement is familiar and the isolated English noun is too underspecified between legal decision, evaluative opinion and decision-making capacity.
Notion is a transparent, high-frequency cognate with no distinctive construction or nonliteral target sense.
Objection is a transparent and familiar cognate, and the bare prompt supplies no useful procedural or argumentative distinction.
Opinion is elementary, transparent vocabulary that does not meet the C1 production-value threshold.
Angle d’analyse fixes the analytical-lens sense and distinguishes it from a future perspective or a person’s simple point de vue.
The English nominalization is rare and contextless, while French postulation also has specialized application and procedural senses that make a single card misleading.
Prémisse is precise argument vocabulary and teaches the productive distinction from plural prémices, meaning beginnings or early signs.
Présomption has valuable legal and evidential scope and must be distinguished from ordinary assumption rendered hypothèse or supposition.
Principe is a transparent, high-frequency cognate, and no context selects a rule, value, scientific law or foundational proposition.
Proposition is familiar general vocabulary, and the isolated prompt does not distinguish a policy plan, offer, motion or suggestion.
Réponse argumentée preserves a reasoned counter without falsely implying the conclusive disproof expressed by réfutation.
Réflexion is transparent and common, while the bare noun does not select thought, a considered observation or a reflected image.
Réfutation names reasoned disproof and earns a distinct card through its contrast with the less conclusive retained rebuttal.
Point de vue duplicates the viewpoint item and overlaps the retained analytical perspective card without a source context establishing a distinct situated sense.
Supposition is transparent and adds no distinct production value beside the retained presumption card and the familiar hypothesis item.
Théorie is a transparent, high-frequency academic cognate, and the prompt does not distinguish a scientific framework from informal speculation.
Thèse is a transparent cognate and its argumentative sense is already represented more instructively by the retained false-friend contention card.
Point de vue is familiar vocabulary and duplicates standpoint; the retained perspective card carries the only distinct analytical-lens sense in this family.
Although the headword is transparent, the English quarrel sense creates a productive false-friend boundary with French dispute or querelle.
